items.title: Splitting a ring over the open pieces of a finitely generated ideal by adding one surjective component
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement is a glueing lemma over the open pieces of a finitely generated ideal: given a ring map A -> C that becomes localization at an idempotent after inverting each element of a finitely generated ideal I, it produces a surjection A -> C' such that A_f -> (C times C')_f is an isomorphism for every f in I (statement lines 31983-31990). The proof is a concrete calculation with idempotents: it lifts the idempotents e_i of the localizations to elements a_i of A satisfying a_i^2 = f_i^n a_i for a common exponent, uses the compatibility of the idempotents over the pairwise localizations to force f_i^n a_j into the ideal of a_i after enlarging the exponent, defines C' as the quotient by the ideal generated by the a_i, and checks the splitting at each generator before transferring to all of I (proof lines 31992-32026). The non-routine part is exactly the exponent bookkeeping that makes all the a_i comparable at once. The final transfer uses a labelled lemma of another chapter as a pointer for the glueing of the local isomorphisms; the construction and all computations are inside the counted span.
